newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK consortium mandates Belcher Gardens loan.
newsitem.headline: HK consortium mandates Belcher Gardens loan.

text.p: A consortium of major Hong Kong property developers has mandated five banks to arrange a loan to finance a redevelopment project in the territory, a spokeswoman for Shun Tak Holdings said Thursday.
The HK$6.3225 billion term loan will be used to partially fund the Belcher Gardens property redevelopment project on Hong Kong's Pokfulam Road.
The project is held 51 percent by Shun Tak, 29 percent by Sun Hung Kai Properties, and 10 percent each by New World Development Co Ltd and Liu Chong Hing Investment Ltd.

The term loan facility carries a maturity of five years and pays a margin of 100 basis points over the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate (HIBOR) for years one to four and 130 basis points over HIBOR thereafter until maturity, Shun Tak said.

The project's gross floor area covers 2.7 million square feet and will eventually comprise more than 2,200 residential units and a 215,000 square-foot shopping mall. The total cost of the project is approximately HK$11 billion.
Shun Tak said the arrangers for the transaction are Chase Manhattan Asia, HSBC Investment Bank, China Development Finance Co (HK), Hang Seng Bank and WestLB.
The loan will be taken in the name of Ranex Investments Ltd, sources said.
Security for the loan is provided by joint and several guarantees of the consortium members, bankers said.
They said Sun Hung Kai will guarantee the largest share of the loan facility, followed by Shun Tak Holdings and the remaining shareholders.
